Controls.Title: Landing Page
Controls.SetLanding: Set this scene as a Landing Page

Notify.LandingSet: This scene is now a Landing Page.
Notify.LandingCleared: Landing Page removed from this scene.
Notify.NotLanding: Switch to a Landing Page scene to add tiles.
Notify.SocketStale: Bivouac needs this world relaunched (Return to Setup, then launch again) before players can use the controls on their own plate — Foundry registers a module's socket when the world starts.
Notify.TilesHidden: Landing tiles hidden for everyone on this scene — press the same key again to bring them back.

Confirm.ClearLandingBody: This removes the Landing Page designation from this scene (other landing scenes are unaffected). Your tiles are kept, but this scene's board will no longer appear. You can set it again anytime.

Edit.AddHint: Choose a tile to add to the landing page.

Config.Title: Title
Config.FrameOpacityHint: Opacity of the tile's frame edge. 0 = invisible, 1 = solid. Applies to the Subtle / Framed styles.
Config.BgOpacityHint: 0 = transparent, 1 = solid. Applies to Solid / Frosted / Gradient backgrounds.
Config.UrlHint: Some sites (GitHub, Google, X, most login pages) refuse to be embedded and will stay blank — that's their policy, not a bug. Use the ⇗ button on the tile to open them in a window. Wikis, docs, dashboards and LegendKeeper embed fine.
Config.WebviewZoomHint: 1 = default. Higher zooms the page in; lower shows more of it.
Config.TextStrokeBlur: On — soft glow, including body text
Config.TextStrokeHint: The dark outline that keeps text readable over artwork. "On" also outlines this tile's body text (note prose, journal pages, table results), which the module setting deliberately leaves alone.
Config.LinkedDocPlaceholder: Actor.xx…  /  JournalEntry.xx…  /  drop one onto the board
Config.LinkedDocHint: The document this tile shows. Usually set by dragging it in; paste a UUID to re-point it.
Config.CardsShowAllLabel: Show every card to all players (ignore ownership)
Config.CardsHint: Drop actors/items on the tile to add cards (duplicates allowed). Drag a card onto the scene to place its token (or a tile, in edit mode). In edit mode: drag to reorder, × to remove.
Config.MeterKindHint: Bar / dial / sliding scale run from the minimum to the maximum. Circle and Token pool count whole units from 0 — there, Maximum is the number of segments or tokens.
Config.MeterTextHint: The label and the numbers can each take their own colour and size. Leave a colour box unticked to use the tile's text colour; size is a multiplier on the automatic tile-relative size (1 = default).
Config.MeterStepHint: Values snap to multiples of this. 0 turns snapping off (smooth). Circle and Token pool always step by 1.
Config.MeterRangeHint: Circle and Token pool ignore the minimum and count whole units from 0; there, Maximum is the number of segments/tokens (up to 512).
Config.MeterIconPlaceholder: e.g. fa-solid fa-heart  (leave blank for none)
Config.MeterIconHint: Circle style only — a Font Awesome icon shown in the middle of the ring, in the fill colour. Pick from the list or type any Font Awesome class Foundry has.
Config.MeterHint: Adjust the meter in normal play (not edit mode): click or drag the gauge/scale, or click a segment or token — clicking the last filled one empties it. Note: non-GMs also need Foundry permission to save changes (e.g. ownership of the landing scene).
Config.HtmlHint: Select text and press Ctrl/⌘+B, I or U to format it. Paste a link over selected text to turn it into a hyperlink.
Config.NoteTextSizeHint: Text size for this note, relative to the tile (1 = default; the note also scales with the tile's size).
Config.NoteFontHint: Pick a font Foundry already knows, or type a Google Font name to load it on demand. A custom name overrides the dropdown. Add more fonts permanently via Foundry's Manage Fonts.
Config.MiniSheetHint: Drag an item, spell or ability from a character sheet onto the tile to pin it; click a pin during play to use it. Rolling still follows Foundry's own permissions — you can only use what you could use on the sheet.

DMScreen.Title: DM Screen
DMScreen.Reorder: Drag to move — beside a tile to share its row, above/below for a new row
DMScreen.Empty: No tools yet. Use + to add a tile.

CastBar.Reveal: Show the Cast Bar to players
CastBar.MoveBar: Move the bar to the next edge
CastBar.Empty: Drag characters (from the sidebar or a compendium) here to add Actors.
CastBar.Exit: Exit the conversation (darken — still in the scene)
CastBar.SelfExit: Leave the conversation (your character stays in the scene)
CastBar.NoGM: No GM is connected, so the Cast Bar cannot be changed right now.
CastBar.NameToggle: Click to show/hide this name from players
CastBar.CondsUnsupported: This game system does not support toggling conditions from Bivouac.
CastBar.CondsFailed: Could not change that condition — check you own the Actor.
CastBar.CondsLevelHint: click adds a level, right-click removes one
CastBar.ImagePrompt: Which image should this Actor's plate use?
CastBar.ArtCustomHint: Used instead of the Actor's own art. Leave empty to use Profile or Token above.
CastBar.ArtWoundedHint: Shown in place of the normal art once health drops. Leave a slot empty and the plate tints the normal portrait instead. Needs “Show wounded states on plates” switched on in Settings.
CastBar.CombatNoToken: That character has no token in this scene, so there is nothing to add to the encounter. Turn on “Give plates a token in the scene” to have Bivouac keep one for every plate.
CastBar.CombatFailed: Could not change the encounter — check you are the GM.
CastBar.CombatNoTokenManaged: That character has no token in this scene, so there is nothing to add to the encounter. Bivouac only keeps tokens for actors in this world — a plate pointing at a compendium actor, or at an Item, needs a token placed by hand.

CustomStats.Title: Custom stat rows
CustomStats.MenuHint: Point a stat row at any value in your system's actor data — Spell Save DC, Initiative, a resource your system tracks — and it appears alongside the built-in rows on Cast Bar plates and Mini Sheet tiles.
CustomStats.Hint: One row per stat. The path is relative to the actor's system data, so enter attributes.spelldc rather than system.attributes.spelldc. Leave the max path empty unless the value is a pool you want shown as "value/max".
CustomStats.NoProbe: Select a token (or set your player character) to check paths against a real actor as you type.
CustomStats.Name: Label
CustomStats.ReverseHint: Tick when a rising number is bad — damage or stress counted upward toward a limit, rather than a resource counting down.
CustomStats.ReloadNeeded: Custom stat rows saved. Reload the world for the changes to appear in Settings.
CustomStats.HealthHint: This row is the actor's health — what the wounded plate states measure. Needs a max path, since a fraction needs a denominator. On a system Bivouac has no adapter for, this is the only way to get wounded states; on one it does support, this overrides the built-in health row.

Keybindings.CastToggleBar: Cast Bar: show / hide the bar under the pointer
Keybindings.CastToggleBars: Cast Bar: show / hide both bars, pointer anywhere
Keybindings.CastSpeaker: Cast Bar: set the hovered character as speaker
Keybindings.CastStats: Cast Bar: show / hide the hovered character's stats
Keybindings.CastInspiration: Cast Bar: show / hide the hovered character's inspiration
Keybindings.CastHidePlate: Cast Bar: hide / show the hovered character from players
Keybindings.CastExitPlate: Cast Bar: the hovered character leaves / rejoins the scene
Keybindings.CastToggleName: Cast Bar: show / hide the hovered character's name
Keybindings.CastConditions: Cast Bar: apply conditions to the hovered character
Keybindings.CastRemovePlate: Cast Bar: remove the hovered character (unbound by default)
Keybindings.ToggleTiles: Landing Page: hide / show the tiles for everyone
Keybindings.ToggleTilesHint: Takes this scene's board off the table's screens so everyone can see the map under it, and puts it back. The scene stays a Landing Page with its layout intact — unlike setting or removing the Landing Page below, which is the designation itself and asks before it takes one away. Remembered per scene, and switching on the Bivouac scene controls brings the tiles back.
Keybindings.ToggleLanding: Landing Page: set / remove on the current scene (unbound by default)
Keybindings.ToggleLandingHint: Does exactly what the map button in the Bivouac scene controls does, without selecting that control group — which would also switch you into edit mode. Removing a scene's Landing Page still asks first.
Keybindings.CastArt: Cast Bar: edit the hovered character's plate art
Keybindings.CastMenu: Cast Bar: open the hovered character's plate menu
Keybindings.CastCombat: Cast Bar: add / remove the hovered character from the encounter

Settings.WorldBadgeHint: A world setting: the GM sets it once and it applies to every player. Settings without this badge only change your own display.
Settings.ForcedBadgeHint: The GM has fixed this for the whole table, so your own choice is ignored while that's in force. It's remembered and comes back if the GM turns the override off.

TextStroke.Name: Text stroke over artwork
TextStroke.Hint: Draw a thin dark outline behind text that sits over art — tile titles, Actor and card names, meter labels and Cast Bar plate names — so it stays readable against any image. Body text (notes, journal pages, table results) and text on solid panels are left alone, because an outline muddies prose at reading sizes; a tile's own gear can switch it on for those, or off entirely.

TextOutlineMode.Name: Text outline style
TextOutlineMode.Hint: A hard stroke suits bold display faces; a soft outer glow reads cleaner over busy or light artwork and does not fight thin serifs. The thickness slider below means the same thing in both.

TextStrokeWidth.Name: Text stroke — thickness
TextStrokeWidth.Hint: How heavy the outline is, in pixels — 0.5 is a hairline, 5 is the default, and the upper end is heavy enough to read as a drawn border around each letter. Drag the slider with the board or Cast Bar visible — it previews live as you drag, so you can set it by eye.

DmTabPad.Name: DM screen tab — edge padding
DmTabPad.Hint: Horizontal gap (px) the DM-screen toggle tab keeps to the left of the sidebar. Increase it to clear other UI docked there, such as a party HUD; negative values push it toward — or over — the sidebar edge.

DmTabTop.Name: DM screen tab — position along edge
DmTabTop.Hint: Where the DM-screen toggle tab sits along its docked edge, as a percentage (0 = start, 50 = middle, 100 = end). For a left/right dock this is vertical; for a top/bottom dock it's horizontal.

MaxWidgetSize.Name: Maximum tile size
MaxWidgetSize.Hint: The largest a tile can be resized to, measured in grid squares (applies to width and height).

LodMinWebviews.Name: Live web views before LOD
LodMinWebviews.Hint: How many web-view tiles may stay live before level-of-detail kicks in. Once the board has at least this many web views AND is zoomed far out, distant web views are shown as a quiet placeholder to save performance. Set high to keep every web view live.

ControlRole.Name: Who can control tiles & cards
ControlRole.Hint: Minimum user role that can add/remove/reorder cards and drop documents to create tiles. Note: non-GMs also need Foundry permission to save changes (e.g. ownership of the landing scene).

DmDock.Name: DM screen position
DmDock.Hint: Which edge the DM screen drawer emerges from. 'Beside the sidebar' keeps Foundry's chat and dice visible; 'Over the sidebar' covers them at the right edge (original behaviour); Left / Top / Bottom emerge from those edges. Also switchable from the gear in the DM screen header.
DmDock.Beside: Right — beside the sidebar (keeps chat/dice visible)

CastBarDock.Name: Cast Bar position
CastBarDock.Hint: Which edge the floating Cast Bar (the character-portrait strip for narrative encounters) centres on. Per-user. It's sized to its Actors, so it never spans the full width or covers the sidebar / chat.

CastBarDockForced.Name: Cast Bar position — force for everyone
CastBarDockForced.Hint: Pin the Cast Bar to one edge for the whole table, so every screen matches the scene you framed. While this is set, nobody (including you) can move the bar, and the "Cast Bar position" setting above is ignored — each player's own choice is kept and returns when you set this back to Off.

CastPlateShape.Name: Cast Bar — plate shape
CastPlateShape.Hint: The proportions of each character plate. Match it to the art you use: Tarot suits tall full-body illustrations, Square suits token art, and Portrait is the original. Applies to both Cast Bars, and the strip still shrinks automatically to stay clear of the sidebar and toolbar.

CastBarTabPos.Name: Cast Bar tab — position along edge
CastBarTabPos.Hint: Where the Cast Bar toggle tab sits along its docked edge, as a percentage (0 = start, 50 = middle, 100 = end). For a top/bottom dock this is horizontal; for a left/right dock it's vertical.

CastBarTabPad.Name: Cast Bar tab — edge padding
CastBarTabPad.Hint: Horizontal gap (px) the right-docked Cast Bar toggle tab keeps to the left of the sidebar. Increase it to clear other UI docked there; negative values push it toward — or over — the sidebar edge. (Only affects a right-docked Cast Bar.)

CastBar2Dock.Name: Second Cast Bar
CastBar2Dock.Hint: Add a second, independent Cast Bar on another edge — e.g. the party on one strip and NPCs on the other. Each bar keeps its own roster; 'Off' disables it. GM setting, applied for everyone. (Shares the Actor size / tab settings with the first Cast Bar.)

CastStatAC.Name: Cast Bar stat — Armor Class
CastStatAC.Hint: Allow the AC (shield) stat to be shown on Cast Bar plates. Each plate still starts with its stats hidden — reveal them per-plate from the bar's hover controls.

CastStatPP.Name: Cast Bar stat — Passive Perception
CastStatPP.Hint: Allow the Passive Perception (eye) stat to be shown on Cast Bar plates.

CastStatHP.Name: Cast Bar stat — Current HP
CastStatHP.Hint: Allow the current Hit Points (heart) stat to be shown on Cast Bar plates.

CastStatInv.Name: Cast Bar stat — Passive Investigation
CastStatInv.Hint: Allow the Passive Investigation (mask) stat to be shown on Cast Bar plates.

CastHideInCombat.Name: Hide the Cast Bar during combat
CastHideInCombat.Hint: When a combat encounter is running, hide the Cast Bar(s) — you're usually on tokens/initiative then. Entering Bivouac edit mode still shows it. GM setting, applied for everyone.

CastPlateTokens.Name: Give plates a token in the scene
CastPlateTokens.Hint: Place a hidden, sightless token in the scene for each plated character, so the combat tracker and token-aware modules can find them — and so a plate's own “add to the encounter” control has something to work with. Skips actors that already have a token, never touches tokens you placed, and switching this off removes every token Bivouac placed, in every scene. GM setting; changes what your scenes contain.

CastBarFont.Name: Cast Bar font
CastBarFont.Hint: Font for the Cast Bar's names. Pick one Foundry already knows (including fonts added via Manage Fonts). A custom Google Font below overrides this.

CastBarFontCustom.Name: Cast Bar font — custom (Google Fonts)
CastBarFontCustom.Hint: Type a Google Font name (e.g. Cinzel) to load it on demand and use it for the Cast Bar, overriding the dropdown. Leave blank to use the dropdown. Needs Foundry's CSP to allow fonts.googleapis.com / gstatic.com (standard).

CastBarFontSize.Name: Cast Bar font size
CastBarFontSize.Hint: Scales the Actor name text on the Cast Bar. 1 is the default size (which already scales with the plates); drag up for bigger, down for smaller. Per client.

CastBarSize.Name: Cast Bar — Actor size
CastBarSize.Hint: How large the floating character Actors are, in pixels. Per-user — size them to taste.

CastSystem.Name: Game system for Cast Bar stats
CastSystem.Hint: Which system's character data the plate stats are read from. Detected from your world by default — only change this to force a different set, or to turn stats off entirely with "Generic". Changing it reloads Foundry, because the list of stat toggles below depends on it.
CastSystem.Dnd5e: D&D 5e — AC, Passive Perception, HP, Passive Investigation
CastSystem.Daggerheart: Daggerheart — Hit Points, Stress, Hope, Evasion, Armor

CastStatDhHp.Name: Cast Bar stat — Hit Points
CastStatDhHp.Hint: Show marked Hit Points on Cast Bar plates, as marked/total. In Daggerheart damage is marked upward, so a rising number means a character is closer to going down.

CastStatDhStress.Name: Cast Bar stat — Stress
CastStatDhStress.Hint: Show marked Stress on Cast Bar plates, as marked/total. Like Hit Points, this counts upward — at full Stress a character becomes Vulnerable.

CastStatDhHope.Name: Cast Bar stat — Hope
CastStatDhHope.Hint: Show a character's current Hope on Cast Bar plates. Adversaries have no Hope, so the row is skipped for them.

CastStatDhEvasion.Name: Cast Bar stat — Evasion
CastStatDhEvasion.Hint: Show Evasion — the number an attack must beat — on Cast Bar plates. For adversaries this reads their Difficulty instead, which serves the same purpose.

CastStatDhArmor.Name: Cast Bar stat — Armor
CastStatDhArmor.Hint: Show remaining Armor slots on Cast Bar plates, as current/total. Comes from the equipped armor, so a character with none simply has no row.

ActorDropTile.Name: Dropping a character on the board
ActorDropTile.Hint: A character can become either an art tile (portrait card) or a mini sheet (portrait, stats and pinned abilities). Choose to be asked each time, or pin one as your default. Hold Shift while dropping to be asked anyway. Your own setting — it does not affect other players.

CastWoundStates.Name: Show wounded states on plates
CastWoundStates.Hint: As a character's health falls, swap their plate to its injured / critical art — or, for a plate with no wounded art, tint the normal portrait. A fast read of who needs help. Needs a game system Bivouac can read health from; plates it cannot assess are left alone. GM setting, applied for everyone.

CastWoundInjured.Name: Injured at or below (% health)
CastWoundInjured.Hint: The health percentage at which a plate starts showing as injured.

CastWoundCritical.Name: Critical at or below (% health)
CastWoundCritical.Hint: The health percentage at which a plate shows as critical instead — a stronger tint, and a slow pulse. Tested first, so setting it equal to the injured threshold collapses the two into one state.

MiniSheet.Empty: Drag abilities, spells or items from a character sheet here to pin them for quick rolling.
